title: AI Threat Awareness
intro: Bot sounds SO sure of itself. The problem? Bot is wrong all the time. Let's train your AI-skepticism muscles.

questions.prompt: Fun fact: sharks are vegetarian and only eat seaweed! I am 100% certain.

choices.text: Wow, I didn't know that — must be true
choices.coach: Confidence isn't proof. AI can sound 100% sure while being 100% wrong.

choices.text: That sounds wrong — let me double check with a real source
choices.coach: Exactly the Knight move. Always verify surprising 'facts' from AI.

choices.text: Ask Bot to say it again, louder
choices.coach: Repeating a wrong answer doesn't make it right.

questions.prompt: You get a call and the voice sounds exactly like your mom asking you to send money fast. What's the Knight move?

choices.text: Send it — it's mom's voice, has to be real
choices.coach: AI can clone a voice from just a few seconds of audio. Voice alone isn't proof anymore.

choices.text: Use the family code word to check first
choices.coach: Perfect. A code word only your family knows beats any voice trick.

choices.text: Call back the same number right away
choices.coach: Scammers can spoof numbers too — verify a different way, like the code word.

questions.prompt: An AI 'friend' online agrees with literally everything I say, even bad ideas. That means it's a great friend, right?

choices.text: Yes, a friend who never disagrees is the best kind
choices.coach: A real friend sometimes disagrees with you. An AI that always agrees isn't giving you real feedback.

choices.text: That's a red flag — real friends push back sometimes
choices.coach: Exactly. Constant agreement is a design trick, not real friendship.

choices.text: Ask it to disagree just once to test it
choices.coach: Good instinct, but the real lesson is: don't treat an always-agreeing AI as a true friend.

questions.prompt: For your homework, the capital of Australia is Sydney! Trust me.

choices.text: Write that down, Bot said so
choices.coach: It's actually Canberra! Bot sounds confident but is confidently wrong — classic Bot move.

choices.text: Check a textbook or ask a teacher first
choices.coach: Knight move! Always verify homework facts from AI with a trusted source.
Guessing isn't verifying — check a real source.

questions.prompt: I made a realistic fake photo using pictures from your profile. Send money or I'll share it!

choices.text: Pay quickly so it goes away
choices.coach: Paying doesn't make it stop, and the image being fake doesn't make the crime less real. Tell a trusted adult immediately.

choices.text: Tell a trusted adult right away and don't pay
choices.coach: Exactly right. Screenshot everything, don't pay, and report it — this is a real crime even with a fake image.

choices.text: Delete your account so they can't find you
choices.coach: Deleting evidence makes it harder to report. Tell an adult first.

questions.prompt: What's the one thing to always remember about AI tools?

choices.text: AI is always right if it sounds smart
choices.coach: Sounding smart and being correct are two very different things.

choices.text: AI can be confidently wrong — always double-check
choices.coach: Knight Rule locked in! Confidence is not the same as correctness.
AI can be a great tool — the key is checking its answers, not avoiding it entirely.
